thread.title: Stocks Lower as Wall Street Awaits Earnings From Apple

author: Home
title: Stocks Lower as Wall Street Awaits Earnings From Apple
text:
Here Are 3 Hot Things to Know About Stocks Right Now The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell Tuesday for a third day. The index ended April with a gain of 0.3%. The S&P finished slightly higher after rising 0.3% in April. Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) shares rose 2.3% ahead of the iPhone maker's earnings to be released after Tuesday's closing bell. Wall Street Overview Stocks were mixed on Tuesday, May 1, with investors adopting a cautious stance as the Federal Reserve begins a two-day meeting and Apple is scheduled to report quarterly earnings after the closing bell.
Markets also were watching the news that President Donald Trump had postponed the imposition of steel tariffs on imports from Canada, the European Union and Mexico until June 1, and reached permanent agreements on exemptions with Argentina, Australia and Brazil. In U.S. economic data on Tuesday, the ISM manufacturing index for April fell to 57.3 from 59.3.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 64 points, or 0.27%, to 24,099; at its low the blue-chip index was down 354 points. Leading the Dow lower were Pfizer Inc. ( PFE ) , McDonald's Corp. ( MCD ) and Merck & Co. ( MRK ) .
The S&P 500 rose 0.25% and the Nasdaq was up 0.91%.
The Fed's policy-making body, the Federal Open Market Committee, begins a two-day meeting on Tuesday with an announcement on interest rates expected during the afternoon on Wednesday, May 2. Economists don't expect the central bank to raise rates at this meeting but many lean toward the Fed doing so when it next meets in June.
Apple highlights the earnings calendar on Tuesday and expectations aren't very high for fiscal second-quarter earnings from the tech giant amid bleak commentary from chip suppliers about near-term smartphone demand.
Analysts expect the iPhone maker to post earnings of $2.69 a share on revenue of $61.2 billion.
TheStreet will be conducting a live blog of Apple's earnings beginning at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday .

Pfizer posted first-quarter adjusted earnings of 77 cents a share, beating estimates by 3 cents, but revenue of $12.91 billion came in below forecasts of $13.14 billion.
The company affirmed its 2018 outlook for revenue and adjusted earnings. The stock fell 3.4%.
Merck's first-quarter adjusted profit of $1.05 a share beat estimates by 5 cents, and the drugmaker raised its 2018 earnings outlook. Shares, however, fell 1.5%.
Under Armour Inc. ( UAA ) rose 1.5% after the athletic apparel company posted break-even first-quarter adjusted earnings and revenue of $1.19 billion that topped analysts' forecasts, which called for a loss of 5 cents and revenue of $1.12 billion. The net loss in the period was 7 cents a share, wider than the year-earlier loss of 1 cent. The company recorded restructuring charges in the latest quarter of $37.5 million.
Ford Motor Co. ( F ) rose 0.17% after reporting a decline in total vehicle sales for April.
American depositary receipts of BP PLC ( BP ) rose 0.5% after Europe's second-largest oil company posted stronger-than-expected first-quarter profit and hinted at a possible dividend even as it continues to pay out billions in fines and penalties linked to the fatal Deepwater Horizon disaster in the summer of 2010.
Boeing Co. ( BA ) said Tuesday it agreed to buy aerospace parts company KLX Inc. ( KLXI ) for $63 a share, or about $3.2 billion in cash. KLX shares fell 8.6% to $71.50. Boeing was down 1.2%. ***
